prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: side impact at intersection in Pasadena, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported back strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1103; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- It is not fully clear where in the vehicle the claimant was sitting.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: On arrival at the signalized intersection in Pasadena, Texas, I found a side-impact collision between two passenger vehicles. Driver 1 was the operator of the vehicle that was struck on the driver's side. Driver 2 was traveling through the intersection from the cross street. A Passenger was also in Driver 1's vehicle. Driver 1 reported back pain and was evaluated at the scene. The reported injury is consistent with the direction and force of the impact. Damage to both vehicles is largely consistent with the collision as described. I could not determine with certainty which seat Driver 1 occupied at the moment of impact, though Driver 1 stated it was the driver's position. Witness statements, scene photographs, and Driver 2's account all match the sequence of events Driver 1 described. No prior damage to Driver 1's vehicle was observed or reported. Records checked at the scene show that Driver 1 is listed on the vehicle's insurance policy. No citations were issued at this time pending further review.
